title: Without Stealing
note: He defines this as not thinking of taking by deceit anything that belongs to others. For a renouncer the thought is as bad as the act. It deals with faults over wealth, so it follows the chapter on faults of desire.

couplets.plain: Whoever wants to be free of contempt must guard their heart from stealing anything at all.
couplets.pm: Someone whom ascetics respect as wanting liberation and not scorning it must guard their heart from thinking of taking anything by deceit. To scorn liberation is to live by materialist books that deny rebirth. Even true teaching, taken from a teacher by deceit, is theft. For a renouncer, stealing means thinking of stealing.
couplets.note: எள்ளாமை plainly means not being scorned. He takes it as not scorning liberation.

links.quote: guard their heart from stealing anything at all
links.reason: Escaping contempt means guarding the heart against stealing.

couplets.plain: Even to think it in your mind is evil: “We will steal another’s wealth by stealth.”
couplets.pm: For renouncers, even to think of faults in the heart is sin. So don’t think, “We will take this person’s wealth by deceit, without their knowing.” “In your mind” is said because a renouncer’s mind is not like other minds.

links.quote: Even to think it in your mind is evil
links.reason: The evil begins with merely thinking, “We will steal.”

couplets.plain: Gain won by stealing seems to grow, then perishes beyond all measure.
couplets.pm: Wealth gained by stealing seems to grow, then perishes past its own bounds. That means that when it goes it leaves sin and blame behind, and takes the righteousness you have done with it. Some read அளவறிந்து and say it knows how much the thief needs and fails to give that much.

links.quote: Gain won by stealing seems to grow
links.reason: Gain from stealing only seems to grow before it perishes.

links.quote: Gain won by stealing seems to grow, then perishes

couplets.plain: A hardened love of stealing, when it ripens, brings grief that never dies.
couplets.pm: A great craving to take others’ wealth by deceit seems sweet at the time, but when it bears fruit it gives suffering that never ends. Because it hardens, it keeps you at stealing always, and brings sin and blame.

links.reason: The love of stealing has its harvest, and the crop is unending grief.

couplets.plain: To value compassion and have loving-kindness is not in those who want wealth and watch for others to slip.
couplets.pm: To know how high compassion stands and keep loving-kindness towards it isn’t found in those who watch for others’ lapses to take their wealth by deceit. Renouncers gave up even their own wealth for its faults. If they then prize another’s and lie in wait, they can’t have the clarity to hold to compassion for all beings.

links.reason: Waiting for others to slip leaves no place for compassion or loving-kindness.

links.quote: want wealth and watch for others to slip

couplets.plain: Those with a hardened love of stealing can’t live within measure.
couplets.pm: Those with a great craving for stealing can’t stand on the path of measuring the soul and other truths, and live by it. That measuring means knowing truly, through perception and the other means, the soul, its good and evil deeds, its births in the four states, the yoga and knowledge that end them, and liberation.
couplets.note: அளவு is measure or limit, and the plain reading takes it so. He takes it as the measuring of truths such as the soul.

links.reason: A hardened love of stealing bars a person from living within measure.

couplets.plain: The dark understanding called stealing isn’t found in those who want the strength called measure.
couplets.pm: The dark understanding called stealing isn’t found in those who want the greatness called measuring the soul and other truths. Darkness here is delusion. Stealing and renunciation oppose each other like darkness and light, so they can’t stand together.
couplets.note: அளவு again: measure in the plain reading, the measuring of truths for him.

links.reason: The dark understanding called stealing has no place in those who hold to measure.

couplets.plain: As righteousness stands in the hearts of those who know measure, deceit stands in the hearts of those who know stealing.
couplets.pm: As righteousness stays firm in the hearts of those practised in this measuring, deceit stays firm in the hearts of those practised only in stealing. Those who have measured the soul and other truths hold to renunciation without wavering.
couplets.note: அளவு again: measure in the plain reading, the measuring of truths for him.

links.quote: deceit stands in the hearts of those who know stealing
links.reason: Deceit settles in the thief’s heart as surely as righteousness in the hearts of those who know measure.

couplets.plain: Those who know nothing but stealing do what is beyond all measure, and perish on the spot.
couplets.pm: Those who know nothing but stealing perish the moment they think evil thoughts: how to cheat the wealthy, take their wealth and enjoy it. To think is the same as to do. “Nothing but” points to what they don’t know: being content with a renouncer’s fruit, roots and leaves and the gifts of householders.

links.quote: Those who know nothing but stealing

couplets.note: அளவு again: beyond measure in the plain reading. For him it is thoughts outside the measuring of truths, and to think is already to do.

couplets.plain: For those who steal, the body itself will fail. For those who don’t, even the world of the gods won’t fail.
couplets.pm: For those who practise stealing, even the body, which is no different from themselves, fails them. For those who don’t, even the world of the gods, far though it is, won’t fail them. The thief is punished by the ruler in this life, and the others can become gods in the next.

links.quote: For those who steal, the body itself will fail
links.reason: The thief loses hold even of the body, while those who don’t steal keep the world of the gods.

ideaLinks.quote: A hardened love of stealing, when it ripens, brings grief that never dies
ideaLinks.reason: A hardened love of stealing ripens in time into grief without end.
